guideposts.label: Pedersen won’t start stage 11
guideposts.detail: “After battling illness over the past few days, Mads will now focus on making a full recovery before turning his attention to his remaining targets this season”, Lidl-Trek announced this morning. The Danish star was second in Xeraco (stage 8) and 4th in Manosque (stage 2). He had won stages and the green jersey in his two previous La Vuelta participations (2022, 2025).

guideposts.label: Cycling history in Cartagena
guideposts.detail: Cartagena has been a stage town in three previous editions of La Vuelta: 1962, 1976 and 2023.On the last occasion, the race headed to Collado de la Cruz de Caravaca (stage 9). Breakaway rider Lennard Kämna won the stage and Sepp Kuss retained La Roja. Cartagena is a classic venue of the Vuelta a Murcia, recently witnessing the victories of Alessandro Covi (2022) and Ben Turner (2023). Cartagena wa

guideposts.label: Local heroes
guideposts.detail: Lorca is the hometown of Juan Zurano, the first rider from Murcia to win a stage of La Vuelta, in 1973. He turned 78 yesterday. The most famous rider from Murcia is Alejandro Valverde, whose list of achievements includes the overall victory at La Vuelta 2006. He won 12 stages in the Spanish Grand Tour, stood seven times on the overall podium (a record) and won 4 times the points standings (a share

guideposts.label: La Roja
guideposts.detail: Enric Mas (Movistar) rode at the front of the peloton yesterday as attackers tried to turn the race upside down. He is the first Spanish rider to hold La Roja for at least three days since Alberto Contador won the 2014 edition. Mas leads the overall standings with a gap of 1’18’’ to Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and 1’39’’ to Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM). Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos)

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Alessandro Romele (5th), Yevegeniy Fedorov (12th) and Henok Mulubrhan (15th) in the mix yesterday, XDS Astana had the best collective performance in Elche de la Sierra, but Decathlon CMA CGM retained the lead of the overall team standings ahead of Netcompany Ineos (42’’55’’) and Visma-Lease a Bike (50’12’’).

guideposts.label: 3 riders on the move: Hayter, De la Cruz, Novak
guideposts.detail: Domen Novak (UAE Emirates XRG), David de la Cruz (Pinarello Q36.5) and Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) lead the way. Siuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) is in pursuit.

guideposts.label: Should we also have expected Covi’s attack?
guideposts.detail: At 27 years old, the Italian is a seasoned baroudeur. And he’s found success in the area: in 2022, he won the Vuelta a Murcia in Catagena. It was his first professional victory and it significantly marked him: “I have a tattoo of an anchor because the finish was at the port”, he said at the start.

guideposts.label: Visma | Lease a Bike leading the peloton
A minute and a half
guideposts.detail: Thirty kilometres into the stage, the peloton maintain a tight leash on the breakaway.

guideposts.label: 3 WorldTeams have yet to win a Grand Tour stage this year
guideposts.detail: After the recent victories of Movistar (Enric Mas at Alto de Aitana, stage 9) and Groupama-FDJ United (Bastien Tronchon in Elche de la Sierra, stage 10), three World Teams have yet to win a Grand Tour stage this year: Lotto Intermarché, Picnic PostNL, and NSN. Cofidis is the only Pro Team with a Grand Tour victory (Bryan Coquard in Xeraco, stage 8).

guideposts.label: A gap of 1'40'' at km 40
guideposts.detail: That's the biggest gap so far today.

guideposts.label: 43.7 km in the first hour
guideposts.detail: Correction: the gap at km 40 was 1'14''. And now it has dropped to 50''.

guideposts.label: 50 kilometres into the stage
guideposts.detail: Domen Novak (UAE Emirates XRG), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Alessandro Covi (Jayco AlUla) and Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) work well at the front. But the peloton want to stay close: 42 seconds.

guideposts.label: The gap stabilises again
guideposts.detail: But it's only up to 40 seconds.

guideposts.label: The attackers are caught with 90 km to go
guideposts.detail: Stefan Küng (Tudor) takes a strong turn at the front of the peloton and then it's EF Education-EasyPost setting the pace. Around 30 riders are off the back.

guideposts.label: Back together
guideposts.detail: As the calm returns in the first bunch, the stragglers brdige the gap with just over 80 kilometres remaining.

guideposts.label: Halfway through the stage
guideposts.detail: The situation settles again, with Cofidis and Visma-Lease a Bike back at the front of the peloton.

guideposts.label: Hayter goes again
guideposts.detail: Part of the first breakaway, Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) participates in a new 2-man move with Larry Warbasse (Tudor). They attacked 74km from the finish.

guideposts.label: 30 seconds
guideposts.detail: Hayter and Warbasse enter the final 70 kilometres.

guideposts.label: Cycling memories from Lorca
guideposts.detail: Lorca is a stage finish for the fourth time in La Vuelta. The winners in Lorca are Italy’s Umberto Drei (1950), Belgium’s Jean Ronsmans (1970), and the USA’s Tyler Farrar (2010). The latter got the better of Koldo Fernandez and Mark Cavendish to take his fourth Grand Tour stage win (the 5th and final would come at the end of La Vuelta, in Madrid). guideposts.label: The average speed after 2 hours: 46.3 km/h
guideposts.detail: It's been a very fast day through the wind.

guideposts.label: Still 30 seconds
guideposts.detail: The gap decreased to 15 seconds but it's back up to 32 seconds as Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) and Larry Warbasse (Tudor) enter the final 50 kilometres.

guideposts.label: Kamna: "I'm back to my full capacity"
guideposts.detail: Lennard Kamna (Lidl-Trek) won the Cartagena > Collado de la Cruz de Caravaca stage in 2023: "It's a special moment for me; or a special place. I think I'm back to my full capacity. Right now, I'm still not like 100% perfectly in shape, but I'm still capable of getting there and I'm really happy to be at a Grand Tour, because three years ago was my last Grand Tour. guideposts.label: Vermaerke and McKenzie hit the deck
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG) rapidly gets back up. Hamish McKenzie (Jayco AlUla) appears to be more affected by the crash.

guideposts.label: The attackers are caught on the final climb
guideposts.detail: Pinarello Q36.5 up the pace.

guideposts.label: Visma-Lease a Bike drive a reduced bunch into the final 25 kilometres
guideposts.detail: A couple of riders tried to attack but Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike) covered their move. There's a small group with Joao Almeida, Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) and Alberto Dainese (Soudal Quick-Step) not far behind.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 3 hours: 45.9 km/h
guideposts.detail: The riders are about to enter the final 15 kilometres.
